citations.assessment: The dialogue on sandal nails names Ifah and Rabbah bar bar Chana. The vessel and the two schools are explicit. Heilprin argues for Ilfa in the encounter.
Rashi identifies the named speaker as son of Rachava of Pumbedita.
The target addresses the brothers and their father. Heilprin’s teacher and hometown inference stays attributed.
The gloss calls Eifa and Avimi sons of Rachava of Pumbedita. The passage itself shows their exchange.
The folio explicitly says Eifa recited Shevuot in Rabbah’s academy and his brother Avimi met him. Their joint attendance is Heilprin’s summary.
The folio says that Rav Yehudah and Rabbah visited the sick Rabbah bar bar Chana.
Rabbi grants both permissions when Rabbah bar Chana, called Chiyya’s nephew, descends to Babylonia. The witness has one bar in the name. The identification with the sick man is Heilprin’s proposal.
The first gloss calls Ilfa a sage. The next connects Ilfa to the Yochanan trade story in Taanit.
The two Torah students propose trade because of poverty.
Rabbi Yochanan hears the angelic dialogue and Ilfa says he did not. The story expresses the time of opportunity in this context.
The Bavli gives Yochanan’s return and appointment by the time Ilfa comes back. The clause does not mention becoming wealthy.
Ilfa sets the challenge. The Bavli names traditions of both Rabbi Chiyya and Rabbi Oshaya. Heilprin names Oshaya.
The elder recites the weekly allowance case. The following segment gives Ilfa’s solution.
Chilfai gives the riverbank challenge about deriving Rabbi Chiyya’s teaching from a Mishnah. The question concerns the sela’s four dinars.
